outcome: No source I could open or find shows any event bearing on this question after 26 January 2024; the question as Shelah posed it (Problem 1.4 in 'Diamonds', Sh:922; Question 1 in Rinot's survey, weakened to CH_λ) remains open. The only failures of diamond on the cofinality-cf(λ) points I found are on proper stationary subsets (Gitik–Rinot, for λ = ℵ_ω under GCH above ω, relative to a supercompact), and the positive results found all add a hypothesis such as □*_λ or □_λ.
problem_asks: One question, for every singular cardinal λ: does GCH (2^μ = μ⁺ for every infinite cardinal μ, as the bullet states) entail ◇(E^{λ⁺}_{cf λ}) in ZFC? Unpacked: (a) the quantifier runs over every singular λ; (b) the hypothesis is the full GCH, not merely CH_λ (2^λ = λ⁺), although Shelah's Problem 1.4 allows GCH to be assumed and Rinot's Question 1 uses the weaker CH_λ; (c) the conclusion is ◇ on the whole set E^{λ⁺}_{cf λ} = {α < λ⁺ : cf α = cf λ}, not on some stationary subset of it; (d) ◇(S) means there is a sequence ⟨A_α : α ∈ S⟩ with A_α ⊆ α such that for every X ⊆ λ⁺ the set {α ∈ S : X ∩ α = A_α} is stationary in λ⁺. The answer is yes if ZFC + GCH proves ◇(E^{λ⁺}_{cf λ}) for every singular λ, and no if for some singular λ, ZFC + GCH + not-◇(E^{λ⁺}_{cf λ}) is consistent. The bullet names no object and asks no quantity beyond these.

events.what_happened: Shelah, 'Diamonds, uniformization', Journal of Symbolic Logic 49(4) (1984) 1022–1033. Under GCH, for singular λ, □_λ implies that the diamonds hold for many stationary S ⊆ λ⁺, including some S ⊆ {δ ∈ λ⁺ : cf δ = cf λ}; the abstract also mentions complementary consistency results. I read only the Cambridge abstract page; the article body was not accessible to me.
events.delivers: Under GCH and □_λ at a singular λ, ◇_S for many stationary S ⊆ λ⁺, including some S inside the cf λ points. Restricted in two ways: it needs □_λ, and it gives 'many' sets S, not the whole set E^{λ⁺}_{cf λ}.
events.remains: ◇ on all of E^{λ⁺}_{cf λ} from GCH alone, without □_λ.

checked_by.qualification: Journal of record; referees not named on the page

events.direction: Partial positive, conditional on □_λ and GCH; says nothing about the whole set and nothing about GCH alone.

events.what_happened: Shelah, 'Diamonds' (arXiv 0711.3030; Sh:922; Proc. AMS 138 (2010) 2151–2161). The abstract says: if λ = χ⁺ = 2^χ > ℵ₁ then diamond on λ holds. The main theorem (Claim 2.3(1)) gives ◇_S for stationary S ⊆ λ with cf δ ≠ cf χ for all δ ∈ S, so the cf(χ) points are excluded. Section 1 lists as Problem 1.4: 'Assume χ is singular, λ=χ⁺=2^χ, do we have ♢(S^λ_{cf(χ)})? (You may even assume G.C.H.)', and says 'The present work does not resolve' it. This is the bullet's question with χ in the role of λ, so it is the source of the problem, not a result on it.
events.revisions: arXiv v1 19 Nov 2007; v2 10 Mar 2008; v3 8 Jul 2008; v4 15 Jun 2010 (journal reference PAMS 138 (2010) 2151–2161). A search result gave 'Oct.7, 2009' as the first posting date; that conflicts with the arXiv abstract page, which I used.
events.delivers: ◇_S for stationary S ⊆ λ = χ⁺ = 2^χ > ℵ₁ whose points have cofinality different from cf χ. The cf(χ) points, which are the case the bullet asks about when χ is singular, are excluded.
events.remains: ◇ on S^λ_{cf χ} = E^{χ⁺}_{cf χ} for singular χ, i.e. the bullet's question. Nothing about GCH alone.

checked_by.who: Proceedings of the American Mathematical Society (refereed journal)
checked_by.qualification: Journal of record; referees not named

events.direction: Partial positive for the points with cf δ ≠ cf χ; explicitly does not resolve the cf(χ) points, which is the bullet's set. The abstract's phrase 'diamond on λ' refers to the restricted set in the main theorem, not to all of λ.

events.what_happened: Rinot, 'Jensen's diamond principle and its relatives' (arXiv 0911.2151; survey, published in Set Theory and its Applications, Contemporary Mathematics 533, AMS, per search results). Question 1 (attributed to Shelah): 'Is it consistent that for some singular cardinal λ, CH_λ holds, while ♢_{E^{λ+}_{cf(λ)}} fails?', described as longstanding and still open. Question 3 asks whether I[E^{λ⁺}_{cf λ}; λ] must contain a stationary set for every singular λ. The survey restates Shelah's, Zeman's, Gregory's and Gitik–Rinot's results (its Thms 1.6–1.30), and Cor 1.29 (implicit in another paper): if every stationary subset of E^{κ⁺}_{κ⁻} reflects, then CH_λ ⇔ ◇ on E^{λ⁺}_{cf λ} for singular λ of cofinality κ.
events.revisions: v1 11 Nov 2009; v2 22 Jun 2010, comment 'Final version'. The version of the 2010 survey is the one I read.
events.delivers: Adds no resolution. It records: under GCH plus □*_λ, ◇ on reflecting S ⊆ E^{λ⁺}_{cf λ} (Shelah; Zeman); GCH consistent with ¬◇ on some non-reflecting stationary S ⊆ E^{λ⁺}_{cf λ} (Shelah); Cor 1.29, conditional on every stationary subset of E^{κ⁺}_{κ⁻} reflecting, which gives ◇ on all of E^{λ⁺}_{cf λ}.
events.remains: The whole question, which the survey marks as open (Question 1).
events.direction: Not a result. It restates the question as open. Its Cor 1.29 is conditional on a reflection hypothesis and does not answer the GCH-only question.

events.what_happened: Zeman, 'Diamond, GCH and weak square', Proc. AMS 138(5) (2010) 1853–1859. The abstract, as it appeared in search results (not in the paper text, which I could not read), says that for singular κ, an elaboration of Shelah's argument derives ◇_{κ⁺}(T) from 2^κ = κ⁺ together with □*_κ, where T = {δ < κ⁺ : cf δ = cf κ}; it also places a restriction on saturated ideals on κ⁺. The author's publication page lists a PDF (ch-dm.pdf), which my tools returned as binary data; the AMS page returned HTTP 403.
events.revisions: Author's publication page lists ch-dm.dvi and ch-dm.pdf (webapps.math.uci.edu/~mzeman/RESEARCH/). No arXiv version found.
events.delivers: Under 2^κ = κ⁺ and □*_κ at a singular κ, ◇ on all of E^{κ⁺}_{cf κ} (per the abstract as seen). It covers the whole set but adds □*_κ, which GCH does not supply. Rinot's survey restates Zeman's theorem (its Thm 1.11) for a stationary S that reflects; that differs from the whole-set reading and I could not settle it from the paper text.
events.remains: The GCH-only version, and whether □*_κ can be dropped.

checked_by.who: Martin Zeman (author, set theorist at UC Irvine); Proc. AMS (refereed journal)
checked_by.qualification: Author is a set theorist; journal of record
checked_by.what_they_did: Published the paper (2010); its result is restated in Rinot's survey (arXiv v2, 22 Jun 2010)

events.doubts: Source conflict on the hypotheses: the abstract (as seen in search) gives ◇ on the whole set T under 2^κ = κ⁺ + □*_κ, while Rinot's survey (Thm 1.11) states the conclusion for a stationary S that reflects. The paper text was not readable here, so I could not check which is right.
events.direction: Positive for the whole set, with the extra hypothesis □*_κ; it does not use GCH alone, so it does not answer the bullet's question.

events.what_happened: Gitik and Rinot, 'The failure of diamond on a reflecting stationary set', Trans. AMS 364 (2012) 1771–1795; no arXiv version (Rinot's publication page). Per the survey's restatement of Thm 1.23 (arXiv v2, 22 Jun 2010, cited as [22]): 'It is relatively consistent with the existence of a supercompact cardinal that the GCH holds above ω, while ♢_S fails for a stationary set S ⊆ E^{ℵ_{ω+1}}_ω such that {γ < ℵ_{ω+1} : cf(γ) = ω₁, S ∩ γ contains a club} is stationary.' This is λ = ℵ_ω, where E^{λ⁺}_{cf λ} = E^{ℵ_{ω+1}}_ω. Per the AMS abstract (search result; the blog post at blog.assafrinot.com/?p=261 is dated 27 Sep 2011 and reproduces the abstract): diamond can fail on a set S ⊆ ℵ_{ω+1} that reflects stationarily often, consistently with GCH and AP_{ℵ_ω}, relative to a supercompact. The survey's Thm 1.24 (also attributed to [22]): if CH_λ holds for strong limit singular λ, a λ⁺-directed closed, λ^{++}-c.c. forcing of size λ^{++} makes ♢_S fail for some stationary S ⊆ E^{λ⁺}_{cf λ}. I did not read the paper itself.
events.revisions: No arXiv version. The date is the earliest I can trace: the survey's arXiv v2 (22 Jun 2010) already cites the result as [22]. The blog post with the abstract is dated 27 Sep 2011 and the journal is 2012. A preprint may have circulated earlier; I could not confirm one.
events.delivers: For λ = ℵ_ω only: with GCH above ω (which I read as including GCH at ℵ_ω) and a supercompact, ◇ fails on a stationary subset S ⊆ E^{ℵ_{ω+1}}_{ℵ₀}, with the stated club condition. This is failure on a subset, not on E^{ℵ_{ω+1}}_{ℵ₀}. Whether that gives failure on the whole set depends on whether E ∖ S is nonstationary (if it is, ◇ on E implies ◇ on S, so failure on S forces failure on E). Neither the survey excerpt nor the abstract gives E ∖ S, so I could not settle it. Thm 1.24 is a forcing result with CH_λ at strong limit singular λ and a generic subset S.
events.remains: Whether ◇ on the whole set E^{ℵ_{ω+1}}_{ℵ₀} fails; the question for every other singular λ; the GCH-only question for the whole set at ℵ_ω.

checked_by.who: Moti Gitik and Assaf Rinot (authors, both set theorists); Trans. AMS (refereed journal)

events.time_since_posted: about 14 years since the 2012 publication; about 16 years since the 2010 trace
events.direction: Failure of diamond, but only on a stationary subset S of the cf λ points, for λ = ℵ_ω, under GCH above ω. Whether this cuts against the bullet's universal claim at ℵ_ω depends on the transfer from S to the whole set, which I could not verify.

events.what_happened: Jakob and Levine, 'Failure of Approachability at the Successor of the first Singular for any Cofinality' (arXiv 2503.18898). Shows it is consistent with GCH that for every n ≥ 1 there is a stationary set of points of cofinality ℵ_n in ℵ_{ω+1} outside the approachability ideal; a corollary separates goodness from approachability at cofinality ℵ₁. The HTML page was read. It does not mention ◇ or E^{λ⁺}_{cf λ}.
events.revisions: v1 March 2025 (from the arXiv identifier and a search result); v2 6 Oct 2025.
events.delivers: Not about diamond. It is about approachability at cofinalities ℵ_n with n ≥ 1 at ℵ_{ω+1}. The cofinality-ℵ₀ set E^{ℵ_{ω+1}}_{ℵ₀}, which is the λ = ℵ_ω instance of the bullet, is not treated.
events.remains: The whole diamond question; this paper concerns a different principle.
events.direction: Not applicable: a different principle on different cofinalities; it neither cuts for nor against ◇ on E^{λ⁺}_{cf λ}.

events.what_happened: Jakob, 'Total Failure of Approachability at Successors of Singulars of Countable Cofinality' (arXiv 2508.02867). In a ZFC + GCH model built from class many supercompacts, for each singular cardinal of countable cofinality and each regular uncountable μ below it, there are stationarily many non-approachable points of cofinality μ in the successor. The abstract page was read. It does not mention ◇.
events.delivers: Not about diamond. It concerns approachability at points of regular uncountable cofinality μ; points of cofinality ω are not covered.
events.direction: Not applicable: a different principle; it neither cuts for nor against ◇ on E^{λ⁺}_{cf λ}.

events.what_happened: Mildenberger and Shelah, 'Forcing Diamond and Applications to Iterability' (arXiv 2504.08390). Per the search result and a secondary review (neither opened): higher Sacks forcing and club Miller forcing add diamond sequences at regular cardinals, with applications to iterability. Regular cardinals only.
events.revisions: v1 posted April 2025; a later version on the author's page (Feb 2026) changes the hypothesis wording, per a search result. Not checked against the arXiv PDF.
events.delivers: Diamond at regular cardinals. Does not treat singular λ or E^{λ⁺}_{cf λ}.

events.what_happened: Garti, 'Weak diamond and pcf theory' (arXiv 2405.03142). Uses weak diamond and diamonds at successor and weakly inaccessible cardinals to bound pcf and to derive some cardinal arithmetic. Read via ar5iv. It does not state a diamond on the cf λ points of λ⁺ for singular λ.
events.delivers: Not about E^{λ⁺}_{cf λ} for singular λ. It works with diamond at successors of regular and weakly inaccessible cardinals.

events.what_happened: Rinot, 'Putting a diamond inside the square', Bull. London Math. Soc. 47(3) (2015) 436–442. Per a search result (not opened; no arXiv version found): for singular λ, □_λ + ◇(λ⁺) is equivalent to the square-with-built-in-diamond principle ◇_λ.
events.delivers: A square-type equivalence at singular λ, per the search result. It does not concern ◇ on E^{λ⁺}_{cf λ} with GCH alone.

events.what_happened: Poveda and Thei, 'A Solovay-like model at ℵ_ω' (arXiv 2509.18991). The abstract (as seen in search results) describes a ZF + DC-type model in which ℵ_ω is strong limit, L(P(ℵ_ω)) satisfies a Solovay-type property, AC fails, and SCH and approachability fail at ℵ_ω. A third-party AI review site says the construction starts from a GCH universe and that ◇ at ℵ_{ω+1} fails; I could not verify that claim against the paper.
events.revisions: The same arXiv identifier also appears under the title 'Combinatorics in Higher Solovay Models' with a different abstract (search result). Not checked against the arXiv listing.
events.delivers: Not a ZFC model of GCH, since AC fails in L(P(ℵ_ω)). It concerns ◇ at ℵ_{ω+1} at most, not the cofinality-ℵ₀ points, and the claim about ◇ comes only from a secondary summary.
events.remains: The whole question, which is posed in ZFC with GCH.
events.doubts: The claim about ◇ rests only on a third-party AI review site; the arXiv abstract does not mention ◇ or GCH.
events.direction: Not applicable as it stands: the model is not in the bullet's setting (ZFC with GCH) and does not treat E^{λ⁺}_{cf λ}.

disputes.summary: Zeman 2010: the abstract (as seen in search results) gives ◇ on the whole set T = E^{κ⁺}_{cf κ} under 2^κ = κ⁺ and □*_κ; Rinot's survey (Thm 1.11) states the conclusion for a stationary S that reflects. The paper text was unreadable with my tools, so this is not resolved.
Shelah 'Diamonds' first-posting date: the arXiv abstract page gives v1 19 Nov 2007; a search result gave 7 Oct 2009. I recorded 2007-11-19.

summary: Nothing bearing on this question appeared after 26 January 2024 in any source I opened or found. The bullet is Shelah's own open question. Shelah's 'Diamonds' (Sh:922; arXiv 0711.3030; PAMS 138 (2010)) states it as Problem 1.4 with χ in the role of λ: 'Assume χ is singular, λ=χ⁺=2^χ, do we have ♢(S^λ_{cf(χ)})? (You may even assume G.C.H.)'. Rinot's survey (arXiv 0911.2151) states it as Question 1 with the weaker hypothesis CH_λ and calls it still open. The two versions are linked but not equivalent: a consistent GCH + not-◇(E) would also give a consistent CH_λ + not-◇(E), so a negative answer to the bullet would answer Question 1 positively, but not conversely. The known partial results are these. (i) Shelah 1984 (JSL): under GCH and □_λ, ◇ holds on many S ⊆ λ⁺, including some cf λ points. (ii) Zeman 2010 (PAMS): under 2^κ = κ⁺ and □*_κ, ◇ holds on the whole set E^{κ⁺}_{cf κ} according to the abstract as seen in search, though Rinot's survey states it for reflecting S; the conflict is recorded in disputes. (iii) Shelah, as reported in Rinot's survey (Thms 1.10–1.12, source papers not opened): positive for reflecting subsets under □*_λ; GCH + □*_λ consistent with ¬◇ on some non-reflecting subset of E. (iv) Gitik–Rinot (Trans. AMS 364 (2012); restated as Thm 1.23 in the survey): relative to a supercompact, GCH above ω with ◇ failing on a stationary S ⊆ E^{ℵ_{ω+1}}_{ℵ₀}, i.e. at λ = ℵ_ω. This is the only failure of ◇ on cf λ points under GCH that I found, but it is on a subset. Whether it refutes the bullet at ℵ_ω depends on whether E ∖ S is nonstationary; if it is, ◇ on E implies ◇ on S, so failure on S forces failure on E. Neither the survey excerpt nor the abstract states E ∖ S, and I did not establish it. The recent work I checked is on neighbouring principles and does not touch the question: approachability (Jakob–Levine 2025; Jakob 2025/26), weak diamond and pcf (Garti 2024), diamond at regular cardinals (Mildenberger–Shelah 2025), a Solovay-type ZF model at ℵ_ω (Poveda–Thei 2025). The Wikipedia bullet itself appears on the live page with no attribution. I read that live page, which is not the frozen 26 January 2024 revision; its wording matches the statement given. AI: I searched specifically for AI involvement (queries 22–25 and 35–36 among others) and found no AI system credited with any result on this question, and no set-theory item in the OpenAI Astra announcement of 1 August 2026 (per secondary coverage; the repository was not opened). Every event has ai.none_found true, which records that no system appears in the sources I read, not that none was involved.
competing_reading: Read at λ = ℵ_ω, the bullet is already answered negatively, relative to a supercompact. Gitik–Rinot give a GCH model (GCH above ω) with ◇ failing on a stationary S ⊆ E^{ℵ_{ω+1}}_{ℵ₀}. If E ∖ S is nonstationary (which the excerpts do not say), then ◇ on E would imply ◇ on S, so ◇ fails on E and the universal claim fails at ℵ_ω. On that reading the question is not open at ℵ_ω. The opposing reading: no source I opened states that ◇ fails on all of E^{ℵ_{ω+1}}_{ℵ₀}; Rinot's survey (the only source that restates both results together) still lists Question 1 as open and describes Gitik–Rinot as blocking one route rather than answering the question; and Shelah's Problem 1.4 is unresolved in the form the bullet uses.
what_would_settle_it: (1) The full text of Gitik–Rinot (Trans. AMS 2012): the exact conclusion of Thm 1.23, and whether the stationary set S's complement in E^{ℵ_{ω+1}}_ω is nonstationary, which decides whether failure on S gives failure on E. (2) Zeman (PAMS 2010), from the PDF: whether the □*_κ theorem covers the whole set T and whether reflection is needed. (3) Shelah's Sh:922 in the PAMS version, to confirm that Problem 1.4 is stated as in arXiv v4. (4) Any post-2010 paper citing Sh:922, Rinot's survey or Gitik–Rinot that states GCH ⇒ ◇ or ¬◇ for E^{λ⁺}_{cf λ}, checked against Shelah's and Rinot's publication lists and the arXiv math.LO listings for 2024–2026, which I did not browse directly. (5) For AI: an arXiv or journal acknowledgement, in any 2024–2026 diamond or singular-cardinal paper, that names a model and says what it produced.
